correctness.rationale: Guo 2014 equation (2.4) is an exact published identity with a reconstructed finite telescoping recurrence; factorial quotient is integral. Legendre valuation gives the exact digit formula at every dyadic height. For small-half indices the unique lowest term is j=1 at valuation 2r; large-half indices are strictly higher and r=2 is computed separately. Thus the normalized quotient has valuation 2r, and the exact central binomial factor adds r+1. Exact code independently reproduces the transform for n=2..26 and the dyadic checks through r=10; these finite tests are not used to prove the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The closest paper, Guo 2014 (arXiv:1404.6978v1), proves the same convolution is divisible by a general central-binomial divisor and supplies equation (2.4), but does not identify the exact dyadic valuation. The new exact termwise binary-digit formula identifies a unique term at the lower valuation. Sun 2015 and Mao 2021 treat prime-length congruences for odd primes and do not directly imply the 2-adic dyadic statement. Comparisons with relevant published mathematical research records identified no direct match; stronger implicit published coverage remains a genuine risk.
residual_risks: Guo 2014 equation (2.4) is very close: another author could have extracted the same valuation as a short unstated corollary.

value.rationale: Guo established a natural global divisibility for this weighted Franel convolution but not the optimal prime-two exponent at dyadic endpoints. The exact formula improves the known lower valuation by 2r unbounded binary digits, supplies a transparent digit-carry mechanism selecting the unique leading term, and explicitly resolves the small exception n=2. The motivation is precision of a published arithmetic divisibility invariant, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
